meaning: semi- (Latin) “half” + fasciata (Latin) “banded”, referring to striking black saddle marks that cover only the dorsal half of the body
description: A moderately stout silvery-grey to bronze shark with a short rounded snout, a large first dorsal fin and black saddles and spots along its back and sides. It lives in bays, estuaries and over sandy and muddy flats, often in schools sorted by age and sex, and feeds on crabs, shrimps, fish and fish eggs.
eats: Crabs, shrimps, bony fish, clams, fish eggs and innkeeper worms
